rounds.proof_sketch: Block dimensions: blockDim=(32,32,1), so threadIdx.z=0 always. Input shapes: A=[1024,4096], B=[2048,4096] → M=1024, K=4096, N=2048. Grid: (64,32). The else branch at line 31 executes when row≥M OR (t*32+threadIdx.x)≥K. Check row: max(row)=31*32+31=1023<1024=M. Check K-boundary: K=4096=128*32 exactly, so t∈[0,127] and max(t*32+threadIdx.x)=127*32+31=4095<4096=K. BOTH conditions always false → else branch NEVER executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes code in an else branch that handles out-of-bounds threads when loading tiles from matrix A into shared memory. For this else branch to execute, either row≥M or (t*TILE_SIZE+threadIdx.x)≥K must be true. With the fixed input shapes M=1024 and K=4096, both dimensions are exact multiples of TILE_SIZE=32. This means every thread's row index (0-1023) is within bounds, and every K-dimension access (0-4095) is within bounds. Since the else branch is structurally unreachable given these specific dimensions, the mutation (writing to index threadIdx.z=0 instead of threadIdx.x) has no observable effect regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutated code is in a boundary-handling branch that is unreachable when M and K are both exact multiples of TILE_SIZE (32). With M=1024=32×32 and K=4096=32×128, no thread ever executes the else branch. Killing this mutant would require changing input dimensions to non-multiples of 32, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should track predicate reachability based on launch parameters and tensor dimensions. When both input dimensions align perfectly with tile sizes (as in 1024×4096 with TILE_SIZE=32), boundary-handling code becomes dead code for that configuration. Consider adding dimension-aware mutation filtering to flag mutations in provably unreachable branches, or design test inputs with dimensions that are NOT multiples of the tile size to ensure boundary code is exercised.
